clinician.final_diagnosis: Chickenpox in the non-VZV-vaccinated girl combined with bullous impetigo and hypopyon sign due to Staphylococcus aureus superinfection on the basis of atopic skin and VZV infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 3-year-old girl with mild atopic dermatitis presented with high-grade fever, reduced general condition, and a new skin rash characterized by generalized flaccid bullae (2-5 cm) with hypopyon sign (transverse fluid level with pus accumulation), disseminated pinhead-sized papules, vesicles, pustules, erosions, and crusts on erythematous skin, with mucosal surfaces spared. Workup on admission confirmed recent VZV infection via PCR positivity in serum and blisters (E002) and serology showing IgM positive/IgG negative (E003), establishing acute varicella. Bacterial culture from skin smear revealed Staphylococcus aureus superinfection (non-MRSA) (E004), supporting bullous impetigo complicating the varicella rash on atopic skin. The patient was isolated and treated with intravenous acyclovir 130 mg TID and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 650 mg TID for 5 days (E005). She recovered completely after 10 days with only residual eczema plaques remaining (E009).
